title: Integration of Cognitive Behavioral and Schema Therapy in Gender Biases Correction
abstract: This article presents a theoretical model of a training program that integrates cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and schema therapy to address and correct gender biases. The goal is to propose an evidence-informed framework for reducing both implicit and explicit gender bias through psychological intervention. Drawing on existing research, we designed a twelve-session program structured into four modules: cognitive awareness, schema identification, cognitive restructuring, and reinforcement. Each session combines psychoeducation, individual reflection, and behavioral experimentation. The proposed model is grounded in a dual-level approach that simultaneously targets surface-level cognitive distortions and deeper maladaptive schemas. It is designed to be adaptable for use in educational, clinical, and organizational contexts. This integrative program provides a theoretically grounded intervention with the potential to reduce gender bias in diverse settings. While empirical testing is still required, the model offers a promising foundation for future applied research.
